//: Appears in the refugee center as a bulk trader.  Promotes production of nonperishable food.
table of contents - these options will appear in the listed dialogue topics

responses.text: I'm here to deliver some food supplies.
I'm trying to put a cleanup crew together to tidy up the back room.  Can you offer any help?
Are you able to buy some canning supplies?
About the work you gave me…
Need any help with supplies?
Who are you?
What's the deal with this written-on paper money you guys use?
The refugees stuck up here seem a bit disgruntled.
Do you know about those beggars in the lobby?
What's the deal with the closed-off areas of the building?
What are you going to do with that back bay area now that I've cleaned it out for you?
Tell me more about that ranch of yours.
What were you saying before that?
I'd better get going.  Bye!

dynamic_line: What can I help you with?

I buy selected nonperishable foods at their regular supply value.  Pick a food to see what I'll pay in Merch for all you have with you.  I'll keep any fraction of a Merch as credit toward your next sale.

responses.text: That's all for now.  Can we discuss something else?
That's all for now.  I'd best get going.
Sell them.
Maybe later.

dynamic_line: Our canning operation is up and running.  I can pay 1 Merch for every batch of ten half-liter jars or five three-liter jars.

responses.text: Sell 10 half-liter glass jars for 1 Merch.
Sell 5 three-liter glass jars for 1 Merch.
That's all for now.  Can we discuss something else?
That's all for now.  I'd best get going.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Ruth Calder.  I'm the quartermaster.  I oversee the food stocks for the center.  There was significant looting during the panic when we first arrived so most of our food was carried away.  I manage what we have left and do everything I can to increase our supplies.  We've got a few growing sources of fresh meats and vegetables, so I prioritize non-perishable food, such as cornmeal, jerky, and fruit wine.

responses.text: Why cornmeal, jerky, and fruit wine?
Okay, but I meant "who are you", like, "what's your story?"

dynamic_line: All three are easy to locally produce in significant quantities and are non-perishable.  We have a local farmer or two and a few hunter types that have been making attempts to provide us with the nutritious supplies.  We do always need more suppliers though.  I buy the foods we can keep in bulk, at regular rates in Merch.  I carry any fraction of a Merch over to your next sale.  For general trade or leads on other food production work, ask the Merchant up front.  The folks at Tacoma Ranch are building up their food supply, too.

responses.text: Are you looking to buy anything else?
Very well… let's talk about something else.

dynamic_line: I ordered food for a college dining hall.  When a delivery fell through, I still had to feed six hundred people before noon.  Here it's the same problem most days, only I can't call the supplier.  Now, if that's all, I've got stock to count.

I'm actually accepting a number of different foodstuffs: beer, sugar, flour, smoked meat, smoked fish, dried fruit and vegetables, cooking oil, preservatives like salt and vinegar; and as mentioned before, jerky, cornmeal, and fruit wine.

We call them "Free Merchant Certified Notes".  We started signing money almost as soon as we got here as a way of showing it represented actual goods and services we had to trade.  Within a few days we'd organized the system, and now it's been evolving into a form of cash.  Internally they're traded for labor and services in exchange for food rations and other trade goods, but we've been using them with suppliers we regularly trade with as well, those that have faith in us.

Yeah, it's a tough situation.  When we started out here nobody was really in charge, and we let more in than we really had capacity to feed and support.  When the dust settled and we'd established a little order, there were still all these people upstairs waiting for a place to live, and no space.  We've set up a little space for them, but it's not ideal.

dynamic_line.yes: I do.  I don't know what you did to convince them to move out, but our supply chain and I both thank you.  I hope it wasn't too unseemly.
dynamic_line.no: Even once we got things sorted out, there weren't enough beds for everyone, and definitely not enough supplies.  These are harsh times.  We're doing what we can for those folks… at least they've got shelter.

dynamic_line: Well, there's the downstairs section, we can't fit more people down there so it's out of bounds.  Then there's the second bay that we were using as a staging area at first.  Things went… wrong.  I hear the security chief is offering a reward to clear it out, if you're feeling suicidal.

responses.text: What went wrong with your staging area?

dynamic_line: We didn't have great organization when we first arrived.  A few of the earliest arrivals set up a triage and sorting system, with the sick and infirm getting set aside to wait.  It's cruel, but we could see there was only space for so many, and we didn't know what was causing people to turn into zombies at the time, so we were trying to quarantine out infection.  A couple folks died in there, and it escalated.  One of the first people here, Jacob, had taken charge of the whole thing.  When the triage area had to be evacuated he stayed behind to make sure everyone who could get out got out.  It was a hell of a loss.

responses.text: Thanks, can I ask you something else?

dynamic_line: Thank you for that.  We don't have any immediate plans for the area.  Once it's cleaned up I suppose we'll let the people living up here decide what to do with it.

I'm so glad we've got that up and running.  One of the people evacuated here had a connection to a functioning ranch, and we got him and a crew out there as quickly as we were able.  We're hoping they'll be able to supply us in enough foodstuffs to make this place self-sufficient and even to trade with other communities as they arise.
You'd be better off asking the shopkeeper up front, I'm the quartermaster.

description: Bring Ruth Calder a canning pot in exchange for 10 Merch.

dialogue.offer: We're getting fresh food in now.  I'd like to put some away for the lean weeks, but first we need a proper canning pot.  Bring me one and I'll pay you 10 Merch.
dialogue.accepted: Good.  I'll see who here still remembers how to put up a batch of pickles.
dialogue.rejected: All right.  Let me know if you come across one.
dialogue.advice: Try a kitchen where somebody did their own canning.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck finding a canning pot?
dialogue.success: That'll do nicely.  Here's your 10 Merch.  Next we'll need jars.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't see a canning pot.
dialogue.failure: I'll ask around for another pot.

description: Bring Ruth Calder a full package of coffee powder (20 charges) in exchange for 3 Merch.

dialogue.offer: At the dining hall I called coffee a staff expense.  Nobody questioned it after they saw the breakfast shift without it.  Bring me a full package of coffee powder and I'll pay you 3 Merch.
dialogue.accepted: Now that's a line item I can get behind.
dialogue.rejected: I suppose I can count stock without it.  I've done worse.
dialogue.advice: Look in kitchen cupboards and grocery stores.  I need enough to fill a package.
dialogue.inquire: Any progress on the staff coffee budget?
dialogue.success: Here's your 3 Merch.  The morning shift thanks you.  Or it will, once I've put the coffee on.
dialogue.success_lie: I've already had one pot of hot water today.
dialogue.failure: I guess it's hot water again.

description: Deliver twenty-five half-liter glass canning jars to the Free Merchants to kickstart their food storage plans.

dialogue.offer: While we've managed to secure day to day food supplies, it's very much hand to mouth.  Our reserves would barely last a few days if something kept our people locked in.  We need a stockpile to avoid that.  We have a bit of meat and vegetables coming in, and we need a way to make them last.  Some of our people know enough about food canning that if we had a good stock of canning jars, we could make pickles and canned meats to get us set for the winter.  Bring me twenty-five half-liter glass jars to get us started and I'll pay you 20 Merch.
dialogue.accepted: It'll take a load off my shoulders if I can finally stop worrying about this.
dialogue.rejected: We'll hold for the moment, but I'll get an ulcer if I have to keep worrying.  If you reconsider let me know.
dialogue.advice: Grocery stores, house kitchens, there's plenty of places to look.
dialogue.success: That's one less thing to worry about.  Glad to have someone like you on our side.  Here's your 20 Merch.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

description: Deliver 20 large three-liter jars in exchange for <reward_count:FMCNote> certified notes.

dialogue.describe: I do have some work for you.
dialogue.offer: The jars you brought will get us started with canning.  We could use some larger jars for things we put up in bulk, though.  Can you bring me twenty large three-liter jars?  I'll pay you 25 Merch.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you.  Once we get a cottage industry set up with some of our inhabitants, I'll be able to start buying these from you and other scavengers in smaller lots.  This should be enough to test out our equipment.
dialogue.rejected: Oh well.  I'll see if I can find another supplier, thanks.
dialogue.advice: Grocery stores, house kitchens, there's plenty of places to look.
dialogue.success: Here's your 25 Merch.  We've got what we need to keep the canning operation going now.  I'll buy spare jars in small batches.  If you're looking for more work growing or putting up food, ask the Merchant up front about Tacoma Ranch.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: I wonder where all the jars went…
